clue.text: Time of life when Dutch pair are within travelling distance

indicators.note: the pair of letters are placed inside the word for distance travelled, so this phrase signals a container

parts.note: mileage is the distance a vehicle has travelled
D is the abbreviation for Dutch, and a pair of them gives two

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the stage of life when a couple from Holland live within easy travelling range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch pair' is not a Dutch couple but two letters D, the standard abbreviation for Dutch; 'are within' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The years between youth and old age are a period, or time, of a person's life.

clue.text: Less of a disadvantage

definitions.meaning: less, as in seven less three

explanation.surface: A remark about something being less of a drawback.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means less (ten minus two); as a noun it means a drawback or negative point.

clue.text: Risky as ground shifts out East

indicators.note: the letters shift out of their order, so this signals a rearrangement of the pieces

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A warning that the land is unsafe because the earth is moving away eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts out' rearranges AS, GROUND and E (East) together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky carries the threat of harm, which is the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Fairy children?

definitions.meaning: fairies as a group, the elves and sprites of folklore
the question mark marks the literal reading: small people, that is youngsters

explanation.surface: A query whether fairies are just youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves and fairies are traditionally called this; read literally, small people are youngsters.

clue.text: Some particle's taken in for analysis

indicators.note: the particle is taken into the word for some, so this phrase signals one piece inside another

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any money'
an atom is a tiny particle; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A small amount of a particle has been absorbed for laboratory testing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'particle's' stands for 'is'; 'taken in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a detailed examination of the structure of something, as in an anatomy of a scandal.

clue.text: Cost dear when a number drop out

indicators.note: the number's letters are made to fall out of the longer word, signalling a removal

parts.note: dear means costly, expensive
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Something is pricey when one figure falls off the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop out' removes IV (four) from EXPENSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is an outlay of money, the price paid for something.

clue.text: Many said to make good living

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, standing for a great many
oral means spoken, said aloud rather than written

explanation.surface: Many people are reported as wanting to earn a decent livelihood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link; 'good living' is read as the adjective 'good-living', virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who leads an upright, virtuous life is described as ethical in this sense.

clue.text: Criminal gang holding American in ancient kingdom

indicators.note: the gang holds the American inside it, so this signals a container

parts.note: a mob is a criminal gang, as in the Mafia

explanation.surface: A band of crooks keeps a US citizen captive in a kingdom of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A inside MOB.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a biblical realm east of the Dead Sea, home of Ruth.

clue.text: Bearing in a bay tree

indicators.note: the compass bearing goes in the horse, signalling one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a bay is a horse named for its coat colour, and so is a roan
W, for west, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Someone is taking a bearing on a tree growing beside a bay laurel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay tree' looks like the laurel, but 'a bay' is a horse, ROAN; 'in' puts W (a bearing, west) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash, with red berries, is the common British tree of this name.

clue.text: Religious early saint is represented

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new order, so this signals a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pious person: an early saint is depicted in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges EARLY, ST (saint) and IS. 'Religious' is the noun: a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a convent who does manual work rather than choir duties is a member of a religious order.

clue.text: Group without a goal

parts.note: no means without, as in 'no money'
a net is the goal in football, the ball being in the net

explanation.surface: A football side that cannot score a single goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a team with no goals; read it as NO + NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of nine musicians, or nine of anything, forms an ensemble.

clue.text: A very quiet Scotsman means to reach Roman road

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name
a way is a means, as in 'a way to succeed'

explanation.surface: A hushed Scot finds a way to get to an old Roman highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reach' is a link. Ian is the Scottish form of John.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ancient route from Rome to Brindisi is the most famous Roman highway.

clue.text: Enchanted by spring time at first

indicators.note: the time word is placed first, ahead of the spring word, fixing the order of the pieces

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
a bound is a spring or leap

explanation.surface: A person is charmed by the arrival of spring time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring time' reads as the season, but each word is a separate piece; 'at first' says the time word leads, and 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held under a magic charm, or simply entranced, is bewitched.

clue.text: Opposed to before, we hear

indicators.note: this tells us the word for before is heard, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: Someone says they have been against it before.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTE and ANTI are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means against, hostile to.

clue.text: Buyers hope to negotiate this large amount

definitions.meaning: a bargain or favourable transaction struck with a seller

explanation.surface: Shoppers dream of haggling over a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is what shoppers try to strike; as a phrase it also means a lot.

clue.text: Clip wing of nasty insect

parts.note: a clip is a blow, as in a clip round the ear
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Someone swats at the wing of an unpleasant bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle lays its eggs in meat and dung, an unpleasant pest of a fly.

clue.text: Note absence of initiative in getting mineral substance

parts.note: B is a note of the musical scale
lack means absence
the lead means the initiative, as in 'take the lead'

explanation.surface: A memo remarks that someone showed no initiative in obtaining a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'in getting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphite, the form of carbon used in pencils and grate polish, is a mineral.

clue.text: Gradually remove advantage on loan

parts.note: an edge is an advantage
a library book on loan is out

explanation.surface: A lender slowly withdraws the benefit of something borrowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To push someone aside little by little, or oust them narrowly, is the sense of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Changing scheduled article to take a new direction

parts.note: an event that is on is scheduled to happen
the is the definite article
to turn is to change direction

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on the timetable is revised to strike out in another direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk or the tide on the point of altering is said to be so.

clue.text: Exonerate Jack and work out the problem together

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is a sailor too
to solve is to work out a problem

explanation.surface: Clear Jack's name and sort out the difficulty as a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'together' are links. Jack (jack tar) and AB are both slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of blame or guilt is to pardon them formally.

clue.text: Bouncy castle collapses without one

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece
a castle that collapses has its letters fall into disorder, signalling an anagram

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An inflatable play castle deflates without anyone on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapses' jumbles CASTLE; 'without' (outside) puts that round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy that returns to shape after stretching is resilient.

clue.text: Applaud good guy who's invested in English cathedral

indicators.note: the good guy is set inside the applause word, as if invested within it, a container signal

parts.note: to cheer is to applaud
ST, saint, is a crossword good guy

explanation.surface: Cheer for the hero who has been installed in a cathedral in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's' is a link; 'invested in' signals the container. Chester, on the river Dee near Wales, is a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city on the Dee in north-west England gives its name to its cathedral.

clue.text: Round on enormous Greek character

parts.note: O is round in shape
mega means enormous

explanation.surface: A huge Greek figure has turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in a down clue O sits on top of MEGA.

clue.text: Butterfly species are at risk Henry found out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Weekend restriction limits a girl

indicators.note: the outer pieces limit, or bound, the A on either side, signalling a container

parts.note: the end of week is its last letter, K
a tie is a restriction or constraint

explanation.surface: A ban on going out at the weekend confines a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weekend' is read as week's end, K; 'limits' puts A between K and TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, a pet form of Katherine.

clue.text: Rely on acquiring list

definitions.meaning: tilt to one side, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Depend on obtaining an inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquiring' is a link between the two definitions; 'list' is the nautical tilt, not an inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone is to lean on them; a ship that lists tilts to one side.

clue.text: Basic ingredient added to a litre

parts.note: an element is a component or ingredient

explanation.surface: A recipe step: put a fundamental component into a litre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'added to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fundamental or primal is described this way, as in an elemental force.

clue.text: Break out occurring in a diner up town

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out in a café uptown.

explanation.definitionFit: A volcano or a riot bursts forth suddenly.

parts.note: to draw is to gather, as in draw a crowd

indicators.note: the leader of the word new is its first letter

explanation.surface: A new chief appears strained as people gather.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'leader's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A face that is haggard and strained with worry looks pinched.
